diagram_math_checks.result: Three C^2 wires, fixed top-to-bottom q2,q1,q0, input |x2 x1 x0>, x=4x2+2x1+x0. Every embedded H, CP or SWAP is an endomorphism of the same ordered eight-dimensional register. This matches alg-qa-exact-binary-qft-circuit Definition and the factorization lemma Statement.

The pictured sequence is H(q2), CP3(q0,q2), CP2(q1,q2), H(q1), CP2(q0,q1), H(q0), SWAP(q0,q2). The first control loop uses i=0 before i=1, exactly as algorithm step 1. Filled dots indicate only controls; a crossing of a vertical connector with an unmarked wire is not an extra control. Six boxes and three control dots are actually visible.

P_s=diag(1,exp(+2 pi i/2^s)) on a target conditioned on control 1 yields CP_s=diag(1,1,1,exp(+2 pi i/2^s)) in control-first order, precisely theorem F2. Each CP_s thus has the required positive sign, not its adjoint.

Step 1.1 and the factorization lemma formula give phi2=x2/2+x1/4+x0/8, phi1=x1/2+x0/4 and phi0=x0/2. Before SWAP the top/middle/bottom factors are R2,R1,R0. Algorithm step 2 swaps q0,q2 only, so the output labels R0,R1,R2 are correct on q2,q1,q0. The middle SWAP connector crossing is unmarked; q1 is unchanged.

The product R0 tensor R1 tensor R2 has basis coefficient 2^(-3/2) exp(2 pi i (y2*x0/2 + y1*(x1/2+x0/4) + y0*(x2/2+x1/4+x0/8))), equal modulo integer phase to 2^(-3/2) exp(2 pi i*x*y/8) for y=4y2+2y1+y0. This is theorem step 2.1, with the output indexing of the factorization lemma.

A standalone Python complex-vector calculation applied the chronological H/CP/SWAP list for all 8 basis inputs and compared all 64 amplitudes against exp(+2 pi i*x*y/8)/sqrt(8). Maximum absolute error was 1.3947004136484323e-15.
